examples.solution_text:
a. Point $A$ lies on the parallel $15^\circ\mathrm{N}$ and the meridian $45^\circ\mathrm{E}$. Write latitude first:

$(15^\circ\mathrm{N},45^\circ\mathrm{E})$.

b. Locate $15^\circ\mathrm{S}$ below the Equator and $45^\circ\mathrm{W}$ west of the Prime Meridian. Their intersection is point $B$.

examples.question_text:
a. Point $D$ lies on the Equator at longitude $65^\circ\mathrm{E}$. Write its coordinates.

b. Point $E$ lies on the Prime Meridian at latitude $28^\circ\mathrm{S}$. Write its coordinates.

c. Write the coordinates of the intersection of the Equator and the Prime Meridian.
examples.solution_text:
a. The Equator has latitude $0^\circ$, so $D$ has coordinates $(0^\circ,65^\circ\mathrm{E})$.

b. The Prime Meridian has longitude $0^\circ$, so $E$ has coordinates $(28^\circ\mathrm{S},0^\circ)$.

c. Both coordinates are zero: $(0^\circ,0^\circ)$.

examples.question_text:
Three locations have coordinates $P(18^\circ\mathrm{N},55^\circ\mathrm{W})$, $Q(18^\circ\mathrm{N},85^\circ\mathrm{E})$ and $R(42^\circ\mathrm{S},55^\circ\mathrm{W})$.

a. Which two locations share a parallel of latitude?

b. Which two locations share a meridian of longitude?
examples.solution_text:
a. $P$ and $Q$ both have latitude $18^\circ\mathrm{N}$, so they share that parallel of latitude.

b. $P$ and $R$ both have longitude $55^\circ\mathrm{W}$, so they share that meridian of longitude.

examples.question_text:
Find the coordinates of the point:

a. $50^\circ$ due east of $(16^\circ\mathrm{N},155^\circ\mathrm{E})$.

b. $40^\circ$ due west of $(36^\circ\mathrm{S},165^\circ\mathrm{W})$.
examples.solution_text:
a. The latitude stays $16^\circ\mathrm{N}$.

To reach the $180^\circ$ meridian, move $180^\circ-155^\circ=25^\circ$ east. The remaining movement is $50^\circ-25^\circ=25^\circ$ east into western longitudes.

The longitude is $180^\circ-25^\circ=155^\circ\mathrm{W}$.

Coordinates: $(16^\circ\mathrm{N},155^\circ\mathrm{W})$.

b. The latitude stays $36^\circ\mathrm{S}$.

To reach the $180^\circ$ meridian, move $180^\circ-165^\circ=15^\circ$ west. The remaining movement is $40^\circ-15^\circ=25^\circ$ west into eastern longitudes.

The longitude is $180^\circ-25^\circ=155^\circ\mathrm{E}$.

Coordinates: $(36^\circ\mathrm{S},155^\circ\mathrm{E})$.

examples.question_text: A town has latitude $46^\circ\mathrm{N}$. Find the latitude of a second town $75^\circ$ due south of it.
examples.solution_text:
Move $46^\circ$ south to reach the Equator.

The remaining movement south is $75^\circ-46^\circ=29^\circ$.

The second town has latitude $29^\circ\mathrm{S}$.
